Playbook.name: AD — Member Added to a Privileged (Tier-0) Group - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An account was added to a Tier-0 / high-privilege group (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, GPO Creator Owners, DnsAdmins, Cert Publishers, Exchange privileged groups) via 4728/4732/4756. Triage question: was this a change-controlled administrative action, or an unexpected principal granting privilege?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Membership in these groups is effectively domain control; unauthorised addition is a direct path to full compromise and persistence.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: Tier-0 group add
Signal.Details: 4728/4732/4756 with a privileged group as target.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Change during an approved window by a known Tier-0 admin: likely benign - verify against change ticket.
Actor is not a recognised directory admin, or the added member is a service/normal user: escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the actor is an authorised Tier-0 admin acting under change control, and whether the addition is normal for this environment.

Step.name: Reconstruct the change: actor, member, group, time
Step.Purpose: Capture exactly who added whom to which group for the change-record comparison.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4728","4732","4756") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.MemberName, winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, event.code | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Confirm the group is truly Tier-0 and note whether the actor made several such additions in a row (bulk grant = higher concern).

Step.name: Is this actor an established privileged-group manager
Step.Purpose: An actor who routinely administers groups differs from a first-time or unexpected principal.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("4728","4732","4756","4729","4733","4757") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS ops = COUNT(*), adds = VALUES(event.code), groups = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Established admins show routine add/remove operations; a principal whose only group action is this single privileged add is suspicious.

Step.name: What did the ADDED account do next
Step.Purpose: Immediate use of the new privilege (logon to DC, sensitive access) turns a paperwork gap into an active incident.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672","4662") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT c DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: 4672 (special privileges) or 4662 (directory access) by the added account right after being added shows the privilege was exercised - escalate.

Node.Condition: INV-01/02 show the actor is not an established Tier-0 admin, or no change ticket exists for the addition.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised Privilege Grant - escalate, likely remove)

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows the added account immediately exercised the privilege (DC logon, special privileges, directory access).
INV-01/02 show a known Tier-0 admin performing the change during an approved window matching a change ticket.
Actor is a delegated admin but no change ticket can be located.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-T0-CHANGE, INV-02-T0-ACTOR-HISTORY, INV-03-T0-MEMBER-USE to the case.

Indicators.Item: Actor is a recognised Tier-0/identity admin.
Added member is an expected admin account.

SOCAction.Item: Close as false_positive; ensure the change is recorded.

TruePositive.Definition: Privilege granted by or to an unexpected principal - escalation/persistence.

Indicators.Item: Actor is not an established group admin.
Added account immediately uses the privilege or is a normal/service account.

SOCAction.Item: Remove the member if unauthorised; disable involved accounts.
Investigate the actor's session/foothold; open IR.
Review all recent Tier-0 changes by the actor.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automation/provisioning tool over-adding members due to a misconfigured rule.

Indicators.Item: A provisioning service account making the change per a broken group-mapping rule.
Owner confirms intent but wrong scope.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the provisioning rule; remove erroneous members.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If unauthorised: remove the member and disable involved accounts now.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Investigate actor foothold; review all recent privileged changes; revoke sessions.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce PAM/approval workflow for Tier-0 changes; alert on every Tier-0 delta.

QualityChecks.Check: Group list in the rule covers the core Tier-0 set - confirm JCB-specific privileged groups (e.g. custom admin groups) are included.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Change ticket verified; membership matches approved state.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unauthorised member removed; actor investigated; Tier-0 membership reconciled.
